package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions distributed via Google Play Store and 9Apps during campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is malicious because it covertly modifies pre-installed applications on infected Android devices to inject fraudulent advertisement code, resulting in unauthorized ad displays and revenue generation for the attacker. This behavior subverts user trust, abuses device functionality, and monetizes infection without user consent.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into pre-installed application APKs on the device

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code scans installed applications, identifies target apps, injects malicious advertisement code into them, and replaces the original apps with the modified versions, resulting in fraudulent ad display.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying other installed applications on a device is highly abnormal and a clear sign of malicious intent, especially when done without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Android apps do not alter or replace other installed applications; legitimate apps are sandboxed and should not modify unrelated apps.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System update tools or device management software (with explicit user consent and elevated privileges) may update or patch apps, but not inject adware.
key_indicators: Replacement of legitimate apps with tampered versions

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected code displays fraudulent advertisements to the user and reports ad impressions or clicks to attacker-controlled infrastructure, generating illicit revenue.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Displaying ads outside the context of the original app and reporting to unknown servers is a hallmark of adware and click fraud.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps display ads only within their own context and report to authorized ad networks, not attacker infrastructure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate ad-supported apps display ads, but not via injected code in unrelated apps.
key_indicators: Fraudulent ad display in modified apps
Ad impression/click reporting outside legitimate ad networks

attack_chain.action: User installs a seemingly innocent app from Google Play Store or 9Apps containing the Agent Smith malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware gains execution on the device.

attack_chain.action: Malware scans device for pre-installed applications and injects malicious ad code into them, replacing the originals.
attack_chain.leads_to: Modified apps are now present on the device.

attack_chain.action: When the user launches a modified app, the injected code displays fraudulent ads and reports activity to attacker infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: App modifies or replaces other installed applications
Injected code in unrelated apps displays unexpected ads
Network traffic to unknown ad reporting servers from multiple apps
file_indicators: APK files with unexpected code sections or ad libraries
Modified app signatures not matching official versions
Presence of duplicate or tampered APKs in /data/app/
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled ad servers
Unusual ad reporting endpoints not associated with legitimate ad networks
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that attempt to modify or replace other installed applications, especially those that inject ad code. Analyze APKs for unexpected code or ad libraries. Detect network traffic from multiple unrelated apps to the same suspicious ad reporting domains. Flag apps with mismatched signatures or duplicate APKs in the app directory.
